questionText: What is application.properties in Spring Boot?

target.learningOutcome: The learner can define application.properties, write safe key-value settings, and explain how Spring Boot makes them available and overridable.

claims.statement: Spring Boot loads application.properties as config data and contributes its key-value settings to the Spring Environment.
Spring Boot searches documented classpath and external locations for application configuration and allows higher-priority property sources to override matching keys.
Spring Boot property binding and Spring conversion can turn external text such as 2s into a Java Duration rather than leaving every setting as a String.

examples.title: Load and assert every property shown in the learner example

validation.command: Run the Java 17 Maven fixture with Spring Boot 3.3.1 and assert the exact application.properties values through ConfigurableEnvironment
validation.expected: The name and port match, retry-count converts to int, and 2s converts to Duration.ofSeconds(2)

visuals.title: Property sources feeding Spring Environment and its consumers

notes: The Mermaid diagram parsed and rendered in headless Chrome and uses only seven compact nodes.
The learner example contains no password, token, or production secret.

review.notes: Config-data locations, Environment behavior, override semantics, and conversion were checked against official Spring Boot 3.3.1 and Spring Framework documentation; the exact values passed an executable fixture.
